time.summary: A monotonic counter in milliseconds, with a decimal part - the one to measure durations with.
time.note: It only means something as a difference: the origin is arbitrary. For an absolute date there is `unix_time`.

unix_time.summary: Absolute time in milliseconds since the first of January 1970.

convert_date.summary: Breaks a timestamp into date pieces, and puts them back together the other way round.
params: milliseconds since the epoch, or a list `[year, month, day, hour, minute, second]` to go the other way
convert_date.returns: `list` — `[year, month, day, hour, minute, second, weekday, day_of_year]`, or `num` when given a list.

type.summary: The name of the type of a value.

bool.summary: Reads a value as a truth value, the way a condition would.
bool.returns: `bool` — `false` for `0`, the empty string, an empty list or map, `null`, and for the strings `'false'` and `'null'`.
examples: system.bool('no');      // true: only 'false' and 'null' are special
bool.note: The two special strings are there for values read from a configuration file, where `false` arrives as text and a plain non empty string would be true.

copy.summary: A deep copy of a value: lists and maps inside it are copied too.
copy.returns: a new value, sharing nothing with the original.
copy.note: Assigning a list does not copy it: the two names point to the same list. This is the way to really have two.

undef.summary: Removes a variable or a function by name.
params: the name to remove; ending it with `*` removes everything with that prefix
undef.note: A tool for the console and for cleaning up, not for ordinary logic: code removing its own names at runtime cannot be read from the outside.

var.summary: Reads (and creates, when it is not there) a variable from its name as a string.
var.returns: the value of the variable, `null` when it did not exist.
var.note: For debugging, not for normal logic: a direct access is clearer and faster, and it is the one the editor can follow.

vars.summary: The names of the visible variables starting with a prefix.
params: the beginning of the name; `'global'` looks among the globals

system_variable_get.summary: Reads from a space shared by every app on the server.
params: optional: what to write and return when the key is not there
system_variable_get.returns: the stored value, or the default.
system_variable_get.note: It is a global space with no namespace: prefix your keys with the name of the app, or two apps will end up sharing a key by accident.

system_variable_set.summary: Writes into the space shared by every app on the server.

profile_expr.summary: Runs an expression over and over for a fixed interval and says how many times it managed to.
profile_expr.returns: `num` — the number of repetitions in the interval; the higher, the faster.
profile_expr.note: It answers "how long does this piece take", not "who is eating the tick". For the second question there is `/blossom profile start <app>`, which measures function by function with self time and total time.
